newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-STRUGGLING FREIBURG STUN BAYERN MUNICH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STRUGGLING FREIBURG STUN BAYERN MUNICH.

text.p: Bundesliga leaders Bayern Munich were held to a shock 0-0 home draw by bottom club Freiburg on Saturday before a sell-out Olympic Stadium crowd of 63,000.
With only three weeks left in the title race, second-placed Bayer Leverkusen will move to within a point of Bayern if they beat Hamburg on Sunday.
It was the second draw in two weeks for Bayern, who have 64 points from 31 matches. Leverkusen have 60 from 30 games.
"We did not play a very good match against the team at the bottom of the table," said Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni.
"We did not play with the right ideas, failed to open space. Maybe some of the players thought it would be easier today. I tried to warn the team about that. Naturally, this is a disappointment."
Bayern, beaten by Freiburg three times in the last three years, were without the suspended Lothar Matthaeus, Christian Yiege and Christian Nerlinger.

Juergen Klinsmann hit the bar in the 10th minute and drilled an easy chance over in the 71st minute. He was replaced by amateur Carsten Lakies 10 minutes from time. Freiburg goalkeeper Joerg Schmadtke made several splendid saves.
Freiburg, doomed to the second division next year after four years in the top flight, also had several chances but Bayern keeper Oliver Kahn denied them.
It was the first time Freiburg had not lost away in eight games and the first Bayern had failed to win in their last eight home appearances.
"I have to send my compliments to the team," said Freiburg coach Volker Finke. "They played well. We had several scoring chances of our own and kept the defence packed in tightly."
Bayern, who dominated the Bundesliga for much of the 1970s and 1980s, have won the title only twice in the 1990s and have often watched big early season leads melt away late in the year.
"Freiburg have done us a big favour," said Leverkusen coach Christoph Daum. "Now it is up to us to take advantage of that with a win on Sunday." Leverkusen have never won the Bundesliga.
Third-placed Stuttgart failed to gain ground by losing 2-1 at Bochum. They trail Bayern by six points.
European Cup finalists Borussia Dortmund, fourth, came from behind to force a 1-1 draw at Karlsruhe.
